title: Bruno (6 October)
hookLine: a well-known teacher walks away into the mountains and founds an order of silence
carry: the cross stands while the world turns

cards: A man at the top of his field. He runs a cathedral school, his students go on to high office, and one of them will one day become pope. People expect him to rise.
Instead, he and a few companions walk up into the mountains above Grenoble, into a wild valley, and build huts. No lecture hall, no audience, almost no talking. Just prayer and work and silence.
The place gave its name to a way of life. Today's word is that name.

teach.b: The word is Carthusian. It names the monks and nuns who follow the way Saint Bruno began in those mountains, called the Chartreuse. Bruno had been a respected teacher at Reims, in France.

Tradition says he grew sick of the politics and money around him and wanted God alone. The local bishop, Hugh, gave him and his companions the land, and they built a hermitage there: the Grande Chartreuse.
Here's how a Carthusian lives, then and now.

teach.h: A CELL, A GARDEN, A WORKSHOP.
teach.b: Each monk has his own cell, really a small house with a garden and a workshop. He prays, reads, works and eats there, mostly alone.

The monks come together in church for the long night prayers and for Mass, and on certain days they share a meal and a walk. Silence runs through the whole day: not as a punishment, but as room to listen.

teach.h: BE STILL AND SEE THAT I AM GOD.
teach.b: The Douay-Rheims gives a psalm line they could take as a rule: "Be still and see that I am God." Bruno himself didn't get to stay. His old student became Pope Urban the Second and called him to Rome as an adviser.
Bruno went, obeyed, and then asked to leave. He founded another hermitage in Calabria, in southern Italy, and died there.

teach.h: THE CROSS STANDS WHILE THE WORLD TURNS.
teach.b: The Carthusians' motto, in Latin, is Stat crux dum volvitur orbis: the cross stands while the world turns.
Bruno himself never lived in that valley again. Up in the cells he left behind, the same prayer went on.

how: Saint Bruno is remembered on 6 October; Carthusian monks and nuns keep it as their founder's feast inside their charterhouses, which the public generally does not visit.

games.q: you're Bruno, settled in silence in the mountains. your old student, now pope, calls you to Rome. what do you do?
o: refuse and stay in your cell
go to Rome, then ask to leave
go to Rome and stay for good
games.why: Bruno obeyed and went, then asked to return to solitude and founded another hermitage in Calabria.

practice: For these two minutes, no words at all, not even in your head if you can manage it; when a sentence starts forming, let it go unfinished, and notice how much of your mind is talk.
If you pray, hold the psalm line, be still, and let the rest fall quiet; if you don't, simply rest in the quiet.
